saw.short: I'm A Celebrity's two-in-a-row trial rule gets its first outing
saw.headline: *I’m A Celebrity’s* “two in a row” trial rule gets its first outing
saw.what: After Tuesday’s episode Ant and Dec said Mariella Frostrup can’t be in Wednesday’s public vote because she has done the previous two trials, per LADbible. The rule says the same person can’t be voted for more than two trials in a row. LADbible quotes the hosts’ account as saying it was “introduced last year, not been used until now”, and viewers are split. We haven’t seen the tweet itself.
saw.why: A rule nobody had seen used becomes the talking point. Fans have strong views.

saw.short: Højlund's 'only one club in Manchester' celebration
saw.headline: Højlund’s *“only one club in Manchester”* celebration at the Etihad
saw.what: Napoli’s Rasmus Højlund, on loan from Manchester United, scored the opener at the Etihad, held up one finger and told City fans “there is only one club in Manchester”, per Metro. City salvaged a 2-2 draw with Rayan Cherki’s 86th-minute equaliser. Højlund said afterwards: “Some good banter… United is my home.”
saw.why: A derby-sized moment in a Champions League night. Football fans love banter.

saw.short: The Bake Off series 17 final crowns its champion
saw.headline: *The Great British Bake Off* series 17 final crowns its champion
saw.what: The Great British Bake Off series 17 final aired on Tuesday on Channel 4, with a citrus celebration cake, crème brûlée doughnuts and a British-landscapes showstopper, per Radio Times and The Independent. Moyin Odeniran, 22, from Essex, won, beating Mo Mahir and Tom Whittaker. Nigella Lawson is Paul Hollywood’s new co-host.
saw.why: The show’s big finale night. Winner chat and family reactions travel fast.
saw.source: Radio Times, 24 Nov; The Independent, 24 Nov

saw.short: Strictly's Christmas special line-up is complete
saw.headline: Strictly’s *Christmas special line-up* is complete
saw.what: Danny Mac and JB Gill are the final two returnees for Strictly’s Christmas special, per Radio Times. They join Angela Rippon, Ashley Roberts, Kimberley Walsh and Lewis Cope, making six celebrities in all. JB will dance with Alexis Warr and Danny with newcomer Aleksandra Isaeva.
saw.why: A Christmas Day-style treat that gets people planning. Strictly stories always do well.

saw.short: Radio Times calls Disney's Hexed a 'lacklustre witch's brew'
saw.headline: Radio Times calls Disney’s *Hexed* a “lacklustre witch’s brew” ahead of UK cinemas on Friday
saw.what: Radio Times’s James Mottram calls Hexed “ho-hum” and says it feels derivative of Harry Potter and Disney’s own archive, and that it will likely appeal to very young viewers. Hailee Steinfeld voices Billie Doe, with Rashida Jones, Jodie Foster and Stephen Fry in the cast. This is one critic’s view. We found no other review or audience reaction yet.
saw.why: Our client’s film gets a critical review a few days before release. Know the tone before Friday.

saw.short: A Dalek spotted in Greenwich is promoting a pantomime horse race
saw.headline: A *Dalek spotted in Greenwich* is promoting a pantomime horse race for charity
saw.what: Metro reports a Dalek filmed on a Greenwich pavement is promoting the London Pantomime Horse Race for Great Ormond Street Hospital. The race takes in five pubs and starts at 1pm on Sunday 13 Dec at Devonport House. Matt Berry and Tony Blackburn are promoting it. The clip came from a Reddit user, and Metro doesn’t say when it was posted.
saw.why: A quirky local clip with a charity link. The sort of thing UK feeds love.

platform.short: YouTube opens custom Shorts thumbnails to all creators
platform.headline: *YouTube* opens custom Shorts thumbnails to all creators
platform.what: Creators can now upload a custom thumbnail in the YouTube Studio Shorts flow, at upload or after publishing, or pick a suggested frame, per Social Media Today. YouTube’s Rene Ritchie said creators can use the Ask Studio AI assistant to brainstorm ideas. It was first available to Partner Programme creators in June. The quotes are second-hand.
platform.why: Shorts now have a real cover image. Worth testing for client channels.

platform.short: Meta shares festive-shopper data from an Ipsos survey
platform.headline: *Meta* shares festive-shopper data from an Ipsos survey
platform.what: Across 18 markets, 37% of festive shoppers use social media for gift discovery, compared with 41% for search engines and 27% for TV advertising, per Social Media Today. Social shoppers are more likely to plan to spend more (49% against 36% overall). The survey covered 14,473 shoppers. Social Media Today says the data was published earlier this year, and there is no UK-only figure.
platform.why: A useful stat for Christmas pitches. It’s resurfaced data, not new research.
